_doc: ROUTES — the INTENDED path through every shot of emberbrook, and every point a player
can enter or leave one by. The legibility layer: scenegraph.json says what the
runtime CAN fire, this says what the player is EXPECTED to do, so the two can be
compared and the difference is a defect with coordinates.
GENERATED by tools/routes_derive.mjs from <town>.map.json (the typed walk edges ARE
the designed route), <town>.cameras.json (which shot owns which edge) and
world/scenegraph.json (the seams, doors and portals the runtime fires). Re-run after
any map, camera or scene-graph change; `--check` fails if this file is stale. Hand
corrections go in `overrides`, which the generator preserves.
COORDS: runtime [x, y(up), z], +x east +z south — the same frame as scenegraph
at/spawn, so nothing here needs converting before it is drawn.
shots: shotId -> { name, intent (what the shot is FOR, from cameras.json),
entries[], exits[], routes[], measure{} }. The key "*" means "the whole scene, no
shots" — that is how a real-time scene (townwalk, a future Emberbrook) uses this
same schema and the same overlay with no code change.
entries/exits: { id, kind: seam|door|portal|spawn, at (where the player STANDS),
to/from, prompt (null = silent auto cut), aim (unit xz: the way the path runs
through this point), seam{n,t,w} band geometry, screen{} where it lands in frame }.
routes: { id, class (road|deck|path|stairs|bridge|ladder), role: spine|link|spur|
vignette|blocked, points[] runtime polyline, connects[] which entries/exits it
touches, source }. role "blocked" is a way on that LOOKS walkable and is not (the
map ladders/winch ship no walk ribbon) — a legibility trap the audit must see.
measure: the offline, geometric half of the audit rubric. OCCLUSION IS NOT HERE: it
is measured in the browser against each shot's own baked depth map by
ROUTES.probe() in public/js/route_overlay.js, because only the depth map knows
what the backdrop actually hides.
mismatch: metres of walk floor whose OWNING shot is not the shot whose camera is up
while you walk it (a consequence of cutOffset placing the seam out on the path).
This is where sgCorrect can fire and where an authored cut lands late.

woodroad.name: The Whisperwood Road
woodroad.intent: THE GAME'S FIRST FRAME. The quiet road through the Whisperwood at dusk, looking north the way Vesper is walking: the arrival clearing behind her, the wood pressing close on both sides and closing the sky, the mossy waystone standing on the verge with EMBERBROOK cut into it, and the road climbing gently away past it toward a warmth that is not yet a village — no roof, no arch, no lamp in frame, only the light on the road. The village is a rumour until the next shot.

waystone.name: The Waystone
waystone.intent: The stone on the verge, and the second frame the game shows. Closer and lower than the clearing: the mossy marker standing off the road's west side with EMBERBROOK cut into it under the lichen and the hand-scratched note beneath that, the road going on past it up the last rise, and the wood still shoulder to shoulder on both sides. This is where Vesper's sketchbook and the waking world agree for the first time, and where Mochi hires himself.

arch.name: The Village Arch
arch.intent: Arrival, and the game's first frame. From inside the village on the high west shoulder, looking back south down the road: the orchard rows falling away on the right with their ladders and baskets, the waystone on the bend, the timber arch and its harvest wreaths at the bottom of the road, and the valley the player has walked up beyond it. The road runs AWAY from camera, so the arch reads as a threshold you came through rather than a door you are about to open.

orchard.name: The Orchard Rows
orchard.intent: The harvest, and the only frame in the town that is WORK rather than home. Broadside across the rows from the road's own side: apple trees in ranks stepping away west with their ladders still against them and baskets under them, the open-sided cider press closing the frame with its crates and straw and the smell of the pressing, and the arch's lamp small back down the spur behind. Emberwake is the payoff of autumn and this is the ground it was grown on.

therise.name: The Rise
therise.intent: THE REVEAL, and the only shot in the town whose subject is a thing that happens rather than a thing that stands. The climb from the arch up to the square, taken from off the road's west shoulder: the cobbles running up and away, the orchard's last rows falling behind on the left, and over the crest of the rise the village arriving one roof at a time — chimney smoke, then thatch, then the bunting, and the Heartlight's glow on the undersides of it all before the flame itself is in sight. Chapter One's beat 4 is walked here.

square.name: Festival Square
square.intent: The postcard of home. Across the plaza from the north, with the Heartlight on its pedestal centre-frame and brightest — the inn's stone steps and lit windows to the right, the item shop and the notice board to the left, the bakery's warm window closing the west side, stalls and bunting around the ring, and the road running away south down the rise the player just climbed. This is the frame Chapter One takes away.

pondlane.name: Pond Lane
pondlane.intent: The quiet one. Low along the shore looking back west up the lane, the pond filling the near half of frame with the Heartlight's glow lying on the water, the jetty's piles in silhouette, the plank footbridge over the brook mid-frame and the washing lines on the green to the right. Frogs, fireflies, and the last lamp of Lake's round out at the jetty.

homerow.name: Home Row
homerow.intent: Lake's round, first leg. Broadside to the home lane from below the rise, the cottages stepping up it west to east — Mara & Pip's at the junction, the keeper's cottage with its herbs over the door and the brass lighter inside, Rowan's ledgers at the top — the lane ending at the hilltop bench with the whole village and valley falling away behind. A lamppost at every door, and the brook running down between the row and the square.

northlane.name: The North Lane
northlane.intent: The walled climb. Side-on from over the pond, the lane running up the frame between its dry-stone walls from the square's north edge to the tithe barn, which is its landmark and its turn — cats in the rafters, harvest stores, and the back lane closed off with stacked Emberwake barrels. Above the barn the lane bends away east toward the gate court and the old edge of the village.

gateroad.name: The Quiet Road
gateroad.intent: The middle of the seclusion, and the shot where the village leaves you. The road curving through the wood with the barn's roofline already gone behind the last bend and the gate not yet in front — seen from the outside of the curve and above it, so the road enters frame at one edge and leaves at the other and a player can read where it goes. No lamp, no fence, no cart, nothing anybody built. The environment shift the seclusion round was measured into the map: this is the stretch it happens ON.

gatefield.name: The Old Gate
gatefield.intent: Chapter One's set-piece stage, and the only unwarm frame in the town. The flag-stoned court from the south, facing the sealed gate square-on with its twin sigil plates in the ground before it, and the Whisperwood trailhead with its stile on the court's west rim. Behind on the left is NOT the barn any more but the wood the quiet road came out of. No lamp reaches here — nobody's warmth does — and after the seclusion stamp (306554a) nothing else does either: the barn is 63 m back down a curving forest road, the village is out of sight from 16.6 m past it, and the court reads gray against a horizon of trees rather than against a village that is all lamplight. RE-AIM AT THE DISTRICT PASS: the framing below was solved against a court at (76,74), and the yaw note's reasoning — Pond Lane's crowns closing the due-south sightline — is about geometry 50 m away that this shot can no longer see.
